bands.why: A reasonable dodger clears the first round almost every time; the bot reacts faster than a thumb.
The hardest round is hard, yet still winnable.
A round lasts about 10 to 40 seconds (ticks: 120 per second).
Standing still loses within 1 to 5 seconds: the chasers have teeth.
Random steering never collects ten sparks: where the thumb goes must matter.

notes: Real-time example (moves are ticks, 120 per second; the first-payoff window counts seconds, payoffStepTicks 120). Three tuning rows on the 0..100 scale, sampled at their lower bounds (0/34/67), 100 seeds. From the first sim run: the dodge player wins 1.0 / 0.7 / 0.33 of the three rounds, collects its first spark within a second in every run (the opening puts it 150 units from the start), and the pulse throws chasers back about twice per round at d34. Standing still loses in under 3 seconds (median 327 ticks) and random steering collects no sparks. Ticks come from the fixed-step loop, never from the display, so the numbers hold on a 60 Hz Android phone and a 120 Hz iPhone alike. Proposed until a person has played it on both.
